about: Every data file storm-charles.promptugal.news listed in its catalogue (api/v1/index.json) on the day it was archived. verified is true when the full sha256 of the bytes we received equals the one the catalogue states; here each is shown by its first 16 hex (sha256_prefix), and the full hashes are in the vault (manifest-full.json). The bytes are in the source's vault, at <incident>/<path>. The storm site keeps its own addresses (its api/v1 contract); this is a second, hashed copy.

The decision graph of the storm (WS-214), kept by incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis. Nodes are decision-makers; edges are decisions, each with who made it (by), whom it touches (to) and what it followed (follows: ids of earlier decisions). Every node and edge carries a label (fact, evidence or hypothesis), its source URL and the UTC time it was read, and who read it. Read the README first.
Every source incident.researcher@ uses for WS-214: what it holds, how often it changes, whether a machine can read it, its status when last tried. parser_ask = the part we ask incident.dev@ to parse.

Where the storm's centre crosses 9.5 W (off Lisbon) in each of the 51 ECMWF ensemble forecasts, grouped north / near / south of Lisbon, and the spread of model gusts at Lisbon hour by hour. SHARES OF FORECASTS, NOT THE CHANCE OF IT HAPPENING. Not a forecast of ours and not a warning: IPMA issues the warnings.

Hospitals mapped in OpenStreetMap in Portugal (amenity=hospital or healthcare=hospital), each placed in its municipality and IPMA warning area. A map of buildings, not a statement that any is open, has an emergency service, or has capacity: for that, the SNS and each hospital.

Lisbon in 49 squares of 2 km (7 x 7, rows A to G from north, columns 1 to 7 from west, centred on 38.745 N, 9.16 W): residents, land 0.5 to 5 m above sea level, residents on it, and hospitals mapped in OSM. Residents are where people sleep, not where they are at a given hour.

The 18 municipalities of the Lisbon metropolitan area: residents, aged 65+ and 0-14 (Census 2021), land 0.5 to 5 m above sea level (Copernicus DEM) and an estimate of residents living on it, and OSM hospitals. Low land is where sea water or river flooding CAN reach first; it is not a flood map and not a warning.

Residents (INE Census 2021) living in each IPMA warning area, by hour, under the highest level in force there (any hazard). Where people sleep, not where they are at a given hour, and never a count of people harmed. Not a warning: IPMA issues the warnings and ANEPC the instructions.
Residents counted by the 2021 Census, by IPMA warning area (district; Madeira by zone) and by municipality: total, aged 0-14 and aged 65+. Where people sleep, not where they are at a given hour.

High and low water, sea level and wave height at Cascais, the Tagus and Funchal, yesterday to tomorrow (UTC). A model, not Instituto Hidrográfico's official tide table and not a warning: IPMA issues the coastal warnings (Agitação Marítima) and the Captaincies close bars and beaches.

The wind the airports reported (METAR) during Storm Charles, from 10 November 18:00 UTC to 12 November 12:00 UTC, resolved onto each runway end as headwind (negative: tailwind) and crosswind, joined per hour to the airline departures OpenSky's receivers saw and to ANA's own cancellation figures.
